offers_products.reason: Sells Dropbox cloud storage, file sharing, document signing and Dash software as subscription SaaS.

offers_services.reason: Revenue comes from software subscriptions; support is incidental to the product, not a separate main service.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Individual plans and a free 2 GB tier serve individuals; hundreds of millions of registered users.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Team, business, enterprise and education plans sold to companies, design and engineering teams, and universities.

recurring_revenue.reason: Revenue comes from monthly and annual subscriptions to storage and collaboration plans.

cyclical_demand.reason: Storage subscriptions are low-cost and embedded in daily workflows, so customers rarely cancel in downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Small, frequent monthly or annual subscription payments.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for software and cloud storage technology, not staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main customers are individuals, small teams and SMBs; enterprise and education plans are offered but are not the core.

asset_heavy.reason: Software and cloud business; it runs on its own and rented infrastructure but is not capital-intensive like utilities or fleets.

notes: Customer mix is partly uncertain, since the site text does not give a split between individuals and organizations.
